newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-off $0.50 -private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-off $0.50 -private.

text.p: Cash hogs were called steady to $0.50 per cwt lower Wednesday in Midwest direct cash markets because Tuesday's hog marketings appear to have satisfied much of Wednesday's slaughter needs, livestock dealers said.

Dealers across the Midwest said hog sales were fairly active Tuesday. Iowa sources said Tuesday's marketings there should be close to USDA's estimate of 110,000 head for interior Iowa/southern Minnesota.

Snowfall Tuesday in Iowa was insufficient to impede hog marketings, dealers said. About 0.5 inch fell Tuesday across the northern third of the state and may reach an inch by late Tuesday, said Weather Express Inc.

Forecasts call for light freezing drizzle to develop Wednesday evening and early Thursday is some Iowa areas, but Tim Bowden, a Weather Express meteorologist, said he doubts it will seriously impede livestock marketings.
Hog prices peaked Tuesday at $56.00 per cwt in interior Iowa/southern Minnesota markets, at $54.00 in Illinois direct markets and $54.50 in Indiana and Ohio markets, USDA reported.
